newsitem.title: USA: Two leading actuarial cos explore merger, venture.
newsitem.headline: Two leading actuarial cos explore merger, venture.

text.p: Two of the nation's top actuarial companies -- Insurance Services Office Inc and National Council on Compensation Insurance -- said they are engaged in preliminary merger discussions that may achieve National Council's goal of becoming a for-profit entity.

"The preliminary discussions will cover a full range of options, including establishment of one or more joint ventures, and reorganization through restructuring, consolidation and merger under a variety of organizational and capital formats," they said Wednesday in a joint press release.

Both companies are owned by insurance companies. They provide research, data collection and actuarial services for a large segment of the U.S. insurance industry and share a significant number of clients in common, performing similar services but for different market segments.
Spokesmen for the companies said their goal is to identify areas where combining forces could improve services and reduce costs for their clients.
An industry source, however, said a separate -- and more significant -- goal may be converting Florida-based National Council into a for-profit company.
Insurance Services became a for-profit company in January. National Council is a not-for-profit organization.

Several months ago, National Council's board delayed action on a proposal to convert to for-profit status following objections voiced by several of the insurance companies on its board, the source said.
That effort was also viewed unfavorably by state workers compensation insurance regulators, the source said, and a merger with for-profit Insurance Services could bring renewed regulatory objections.
"They may have some jitters over this," the source said.
The companies said it is not certain that a merger or alliance would result in National Council changing its not-for-profit status.
"It is not a forgone conclusion that they would become a for-profit company in a merger or alliance," said Insurance Services spokesman David Ostwald.

Meanwhile, National Council has become increasingly vulnerable to for-profit competitors in the workers compensation insurance support services market that it has dominated for decades, according to trade press reports.
A merger of the two would bolster their positions, but in particular would "make Insurance Services more dominant than it already is," the source said.
Insurance Services is working to close by early September its acquisition of American Insurance Services Group, another move that would significantly expand its range of services, Ostwald said.
Insurance Services, a New York company operating in all 50 states, primarily estimates future claims losses on about 15 lines of commercial and personal lines of property and casualty insurance.
Its main line of business covers the commercial and personal property and automobile lines of insurance, and it had 1996 revenues of $247 million, Ostwald said.

National Council sets rates for workers compensation insurance for 37 states and provides other actuarial and research services for providers of workers compensation insurance, spokesman Alan Macher said. It had 1996 revenues of $134 million.

The companies have no timeline for completing the talks, they said. Any joint action would require approval of both companies boards of directors, National Council's membership and Insurance Services' shareholders.
